title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XVII: Garissoles — communem & singularem; Bernard; conception
pass_a_gloss: GAR. For thus it would nearly make equals with that distinction of imputation into common and singular which we premised: so that we would understand the prior and immediate as that common which we said; the posterior and mediate as that which we named proper or singular. For certainly that common or immediate, just as it was posterior to Adam's first actual transgression, so was prior to the personal existence of each man sprung from Adam, and so also to that corruption which descends into individuals by natural generation; insofar as from the beginning all things were commonly in Adam, in which sense it was said by Bernard that Adam and Eve were our destroyers before they were parents. But singular, proper, personal and mediate imputation may rightly be called posterior to the corruption inherent in us, insofar as that sin can be imputed to no one personally unless he is a son of Adam, and so unless he exists personally: nor can anyone exist personally and be held for a son of Adam unless after soul and body have coalesced into one person: which coalescence and conjunction of the essential parts of man is without doubt posterior to conception and so on. Therefore in first conception the soul is not yet present, he is not yet a man, not yet a son of Adam: and yet from the very moment of conception viciousness is in the seed, inasmuch as it has that tinder of sin which they define as a disordered quality of the flesh drawn from the sin of the first parents into posterity, and so on.
pass_b_english: Garissoles (§XVII): For that would nearly match the distinction we already set out into common and singular imputation: taking the prior and immediate as that common imputation we named, and the posterior and mediate as what we called proper or singular. That common or immediate imputation, though later than Adam's first actual transgression, was earlier than each person sprung from Adam's personal existence—and earlier also than the corruption that descends on each by natural generation—insofar as from the beginning all were commonly in Adam. In that sense Bernard said Adam and Eve were our destroyers before they were our parents. But singular, proper, personal, mediate imputation may rightly be called later than the corruption inherent in us, since that sin can be charged to no one personally unless he is Adam's son and so exists as a person; and no one exists as a person and counts as Adam's son until soul and body have coalesced into one person—which union of the essential parts of man is without doubt later than conception, and so on. Therefore at first conception the soul is not yet present; there is not yet a man, not yet a son of Adam; and yet from the very moment of conception viciousness is in the seed, which has that tinder of sin they define as a disordered quality of the flesh drawn from the first parents' sin into their posterity, and so on.
source_text: GAR. Ita enim paria ferme faceret cum ea, quam praemisimus, imputationis distinctione in communem & singularem: ut priorem & immediatam intelligeremus, communem illam quam diximus; posteriorem & mediatam quam propriam sive singularem nominavimus. Nam certe communis illa sive immediata, quemadmodum posterior fuit prima actuali Adae transgressione, ita prior fuit personali cujusque hominis ex Adamo prognati existentia, atque adeo etiam corruptione illa, quae in singulos naturali generatione descendit; quatenus ab initio res fuerunt omnes communiter in Adamo, quo sensu dictum est a Bernardo, Adamum & Evam fuisse prius nostros peremptores quam parentes. At imputatio singularis, propria, personalis & mediata, recte dici possit corruptione nobis inhaerente posterior, quatenus nemini personaliter imputari potest peccatum istud, nisi filius sit Adami, adeoque nisi personaliter existat: neque potest aliquis personaliter existere, & pro filio Adami haberi, nisi postquam anima & corpus in unam personam coaluerunt: quae partium hominis essentialium coalitio atque conjunctio, sine dubio conceptione posterior est &c. Ergo in conceptione prima nondum adest anima, nondum homo est, nondum filius Adami: & tamen ab ipso conceptionis momento inest vitiositas in semine, quippe quod habet fomitem illum peccati, quem definiunt, inordinatam carnis qualitatem ex peccato primorum parentium traductam in posteros, &c.
